title: Flashcards Are Not a Study Method
hook: Flashcards are not a study method.
cta: What makes a flashcard useful to you?

slides.label: STUDY COURT #02
slides.title: FLASHCARDS ARE NOT
slides.body: They are a tool. What you ask your brain to do with them decides whether you learn.
slides.footer: THE COURT IS NOW IN SESSION

slides.label: THE ACCUSATION
slides.title: Most cards test
slides.body: You see a familiar prompt, flip quickly, and think: “I knew that.” Familiarity can feel like knowledge without proving recall.

slides.label: THE EVIDENCE
slides.title: The flip speed
slides.body: Flip immediately and the answer becomes a recognition cue. Wait, retrieve, and explain first—and the card becomes active practice.

slides.label: BAD CARD
slides.title: One word in.
slides.body: Tiny fact pairs can help with vocabulary. But they often hide relationships, reasoning, and when an idea should be used.
slides.callout: A CORRECT WORD IS NOT ALWAYS UNDERSTANDING

slides.label: BETTER CARD
slides.title: Make your brain
slides.body: Ask for an explanation, an example, a comparison, or the next step in a problem—before looking at the answer.

slides.label: THE DEFENSE
slides.title: Flashcards can be
slides.body: They make retrieval repeatable and easy to space. The problem is not the card—it is passive use and shallow prompts.
slides.callout: GOOD TOOL. NOT AUTOMATICALLY GOOD LEARNING.

slides.label: THE VERDICT
slides.title: Do not count
slides.body: Count what you can retrieve, explain, and use without seeing the back. That is the performance that matters.

slides.label: THE JURY
slides.title: Overrated—
slides.body: What makes a flashcard genuinely useful to you?
slides.footer: SAVE THIS BEFORE YOUR NEXT REVIEW
